The Abbeyglen Castle Hotel in Clifden, Connemara provides beautiful stylish accommodation which makes us one of the best places to stay in Ireland! Each bedroom has a classic feel and each room has its own character.
Our Beautiful, Luxury Suites are bound to make you feel like a King or Queen of the Castle so why not book that 4 Star Luxury Accommodation and treat yourself to this amazing experience!
Each room offers all the services you expect from a superior hotel including, Multi-channel television, Iron and Trouser Press, Hairdryer, Tea / Coffee making facilities, Complimentary Toiletries, Complimentary Bottled Water and all have classic en suite bathroom and shower facilities.
Choose from a selection of room types to suit you and your personality, from our Original Rooms, Standard Rooms, Superior Rooms and the beautiful Castle Suites. Charming and varied and reflecting the individuality of the Castle, the rooms and suites each have their own character and some of our Superior Rooms and Castle Suites have four poster beds, open fires and relaxing, free-standing claw-foot baths.
When booking either a Superior Room or a Castle Suite, be sure to mention in the Special Requests Box if you would like one of the features listed above as not all Superior Rooms and Castle Suites come with these features. We will do our utmost to satisfy your individual requests.

Frequently Asked Questions
Where to stay in Clifden, Connemara for sightseeing?
Abbeyglen Castle Hotel is the perfect hotel located on the Sky Road. The hotel is only a 5 minute drive from the Sky Road viewing point which showcases the most spectacular panoramic views over Clifden Bay and its offshore islands. The hotel is a 5 minute walk from Clifden town.
What is the different type of rooms at Abbeyglen Castle?
Abbeyglen Castle Four Star Hotel offers Original Rooms, Standard Rooms, Superior Rooms and Luxury Castle Suites. The sizing of the rooms vary. Our Superior Rooms and Castle Suites are both very spacious. Our Superior Rooms and Castle Suites have different features such as claw foot baths, fireplaces and 4 poster beds. Not all of the rooms have these features.
How do I find a luxury hotel room in Connemara?
Abbeyglen Castle Hotel offers luxury bedrooms such as our Superior Rooms and Castle Suites. You will not be disappointed when you book a stay at Abbeyglen Castle Hotel and stay in one of our luxury hotel suites in Clifden.
Is parking available at Abbeyglen Castle?
Abbeyglen Castle Hotel offers Free Car Parking. There is a lot of parking available and reservations are not needed.
What is check-in and check-out time at Abbeyglen Castle in Connemara?
Check-in time at Abbeyglen Castle Hotel is from 3pm. Check-out time at Abbeyglen Castle Hotel is 12 noon. Should a guest arrive to the hotel earlier than 3pm and if the room is ready, we are more than happy to check the guests in early. If guests check-in and the room is not ready, we are more than happy to store the luggage until the room is ready. Should guests require a late check-out, there is a late check-out fee for €20 and this allows the guest to stay in the room until 1pm.
What are the best hotels with balconies in Connemara?
Abbeyglen Castle Hotel has one room that has a balcony. This is one of our superior rooms and is available on request.
Has Abbeyglen Castle in Clifden rooms with great views?
Abbeyglen Castle Hotel has beautiful views of the Twelve Bens Mountain Range and Clifden Bay. There are also stunning views of the gardens at the front of the hotel. Don’t miss out our hotel rooms with great view in Connemara.
Why is the water at the hotel yellow or brown?
Being located on the Sky Road gives the Abbeyglen access to organic Bog (Peat) water. Which comes from a remote isolated lake located on the mountain behind the hotel.
Bog(Peat) water contains many natural minerals which have been scientifically proven to reduce signs of ageing and contains healing properties. Organic bog water contains the following minerals; Zinc, Copper, Iron and Selonium. Zinc has anti inflammatory properties and reduces skin inflammations such as eczema. Copper contains anti-bacterial and anti-fungal properties. Iron has been proven to aid with skin healing and selenium ensures that the skin remains firm and protected.

The Treatment Rooms at Abbeyglen Castle Hotel offer spa treatments such as Indian Head Massage, Full Body Massage, Back, Neck and Shoulder Massage and Hot Stone Massage. They also offer Elemis Signature Facials, Crystal Clear Microdermabrasion and much more.

The History of Abbeyglen Castle, Clifden
History
Abbeyglen Castle
Abbeyglen Castle was built in 1832 by John d'Arcy of Clifden Castle. It was leased to the then parish priest as Glenowen House. In 1854, it was bought by the Irish Church Mission Society for use as a Protestant Orphanage. It was here the girls were trained for domestic service. The Connemara Orphan Nurseries operated until 1955 when it closed due to financial difficulties. In its final years it became a mixed orphanage with, for example, seven boys and four girls in 1953. These were supported by donations from local patrons plus various investments. After its closure, the building fell derelict and was home to cattle and sheep for some time. The property was purchased by Mr. Padraig Joyce of Clifden and he and his wife operated the Glenowen House Hotel in the 1960's. The Hughes family interest began in 1969 and, since then they have developed Abbeyglen Castle into one of Connemara's premier hotels .
The Old Clifden Pier
The Old Clifden Pier is located south of the Castle's grounds. Plans were drawn up for this quay in 1822 by Alexander Nimmo, the then newly appointed engineer for the Western District. (He was also responsible for many of the roads in West Connemara and for laying out the village of roundstone). Due to many delays, the quay was not completed until 1831. For some years, as Clifden prospered, the quay saw ships from London, Liverpool and other English trading ports. However, because of its tidal nature, Clifden quay lost its business to other ports. During its heyday, many goods were exported, mainly wheat, plus fish, seaweed, etc. Imports included salt, hemp, and iron.
The d'Arcy Monument
The d'Arcy Monument is located to the west of the Castle's grounds. John d'arcy, the founder of Clifden and the builder of Clifden Castle, died in 1839. In that same year, work was begun on a monument in his memory. Although local folklore says d'Arcy himself began such a memorial, it is likely that the project was instigated by the first citizens of Clifden. The work was not completed due to lack of funds. Records show another attempt was made to finish construction in 1870, but this failed also. The monument remained incomplete until the spring of 1992 when the local heritage restored and capped the monument.
Clifden Castle
One mile up the Sky Road is the entrance to Clifden Castle . The castle was built by John d'arcy between 1812 and 1815. It was the first building of an ambitious scheme to found a new town, Clifden. The d'Arcy estate prospered for about 30 years but, along with many others, was financially ruined by the Great Famine of 1845/48. The castle then passed to the Eyre family of Bath who held mortgages on the estate. The Eyres opened the burial ground north of the castle and interred three of their children there. Tenants were also allowed to bury their infants there. After the death in 1894 of the last Eyre occupier, the castle was abandoned and since then has fallen into ruin.

wikipedia.title: Замок Аббейглен
wikipedia.extract: Замок Аббейглен — один із замків Ірландії. Розташований в графстві Ґолвей. Замок розташований в мальовничій гірській долині біля селищ Кліфден та Коннемара. Нині в замку готель. З вікон замку відкривається мальовничий вид на затоку Кліфден, замок розташований біля мальовничих скелястих гір Дванадцять Бенів. Замок користується величезною популярністю серед туристів.
